extracted.intended_audience: general readers of entertainment/TV news and streaming audiences
extracted.subtask_description: A short-form entertainment news article describing a TV episode's removal and reinstatement on a streaming platform due to racially problematic content. Focuses on platform decisions, examples of offending content, and broader industry reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of blackface/brownface/other racially stereotypical portrayals
rubrics_metrics.description: Episodes were removed from streaming because they featured blackface, brownface, yellowface, or other overtly stereotypical and racist characterizations (examples: the gang wearing blackface to play Roger Murtaugh; Dee playing Martina Martinez and Taiwan Tammy using brown and yellowface).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platforms have considered these portrayals unacceptable and grounds for pulling episodes; the article cites multiple shows and episodes removed in summer 2020 for similar reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context, intent, and self-aware satire as a mitigating factor
rubrics_metrics.description: A show's apparent self-awareness or the idea that the program is 'in on its own joke' may be used by platforms or rights-holders to justify returning controversial episodes to libraries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece notes it’s unclear whether Hulu/FX decided the episode’s return was defensible because the show was mocking the behavior or because its age made decision-makers more comfortable — indicating context/intent and historical distance can influence platform decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective removal versus retention across episodes and releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Platforms may remove some episodes from streaming while leaving others; some episodes may also be omitted from physical releases (e.g., DVDs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article documents that five installments were pulled but one (season 4 episode 3) was quietly returned while other episodes remain off streaming and an episode ('Dee Day') was not included on the DVD release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of content warnings as an alternative to removal
rubrics_metrics.description: Platforms may opt to keep older problematic content available but add contextual content warnings rather than removing it outright.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given: Disney+ rolled out content warnings for older movies that 'did not age well' as an alternative approach to outright removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform decisions influenced by social and cultural events
rubrics_metrics.description: Broader social movements and heightened scrutiny (e.g., the protests following George Floyd's death) can trigger reviews and removals of content deemed racially insensitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article ties the June 2020 removals to 'heightened scrutiny to racist portrayals sparked in large part by racial justice protests centered on the death of George Floyd.'
